runtime.command_template: python tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <libpinmame> --game <driver> --rom-path <vpinmame-roms> --work-dir <new-isolated-state> --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/stern/<scenario>.json --output <external-run.json>, for the eight nineball runs (self-test, solenoid-test, switch-test, gameplay, game-over-and-slam, kick-out-spot, lock-lane, spinner-option) and one run each of ninebafp and ninebalb. ROM archives: nineball 4311155374bd000db727c74747cfec8707755a899e5bfd25cc35c133851da971, ninebafp 48ff10c6b97ca72bd9cffa2768d442bdf0cac8f98020d3a51ba4ec0c9803acac, ninebalb 21543f3f65d5f80f1892e34881c7ff1087f9dc3a285f8b8c14e8dacce62ed2bc. Each scenario starts with a 25 s wait for the ROM's power-up test. Each set_switch or pulse is a host stimulus, never a ROM observation; display readings are player 1's seven-segment words read as digits.

game-over-and-slam.note: Three balls are served, scored on the pop bumper and drained until game over, a second game is started and the slam switch (public 8) is closed. The power-up initialisation pulses the continuous and kick-out outputs once each: public 8 at 11.26 s, public 17 at 6.22 s, public 18 at 6.22 s, public 19 at 6.22 s, public 20 at 6.22 s.

gameplay.limitation: From the step `eight bank: object 1 (sw9) raised` on, this run raised the eight-bank targets without modelling the reset and knock-down coils, and once the kick-out hole closed the ROM began retrying public 9 (object 7's knock-down coil) every 0.80 s (median) while it waited for switch 15, which the run never closed. Public 9 and the bank coils in every later action are that retry, not a response to the action; the flipper outputs 45-48, the tilt's drop of 19 and its pulse of 8 are read beside it. The retained kick-out-spot and lock-lane runs model the targets and are the evidence for the knock-down and spot behaviour.

self-test.limitation: The burn-in drives the displays with test frames, so the driver numbers are read from the solenoid-test run instead.
self-test.note: One Self Test press starts the burn-in test. All sixty lamp addresses (60 seen) are driven and the four decoder holes 16, 32, 48 and 64 never are; the solenoids fire in a repeating 19-step cycle that starts with public 1.

solenoid-test.note: Four accepted Self Test presses start the solenoid test, which pulses one driver at a time and shows its number on the player displays (read 0.25 s after each pulse; every frame read is pinned in the frame-readings seed). The ROM ignored press 1 of the first step, made 27.0 s into the run, so the scenario repeated it until the burn-in's first pulse appeared. Over 4 complete cycles, driver numbers 1-19 pair with public addresses 1->2, 2->1, 3->6, 4->7, 5->3, 6->4, 7->5, 8->8, 9->11, 10->12, 11->14, 12->13, 13->9, 14->10, 15->19, 16->15, 17->17, 18->20, 19->18.

spinner-option.note: Option switch 17 at PinMAME's default (every option switch OFF; the same default gives the three-ball games of the other runs, which the manual prints as switch 7 OFF). With a game started, the three-bank targets are held down one at a time; the spinner value lamps (public 12, 28, 44 and 60) that came on at each step: center bank: center target 19 down -> [12]; right bank: center target 23 down -> [28]; center bank: outside target 18 down -> []; center bank: outside target 20 down completes the center bank -> []; right bank: outside target 22 down -> []; right bank: outside target 24 down completes both three-target banks -> [44, 60]. The last step completes both banks and the ROM pulses both bank resets while the host keeps every target down, so its lamps are not attributed to one target.
